subject: Recap & next steps: on-prem control-plane interoperability (post-demo)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Grant <sophia@finopsinc.com>, FinOps TechOps <ops@finopsinc.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap & next steps: on-prem control-plane interoperability (post-demo)

Hi Sophia / team,

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key takeaways from the demo
- Priority requirements: full VPC isolation for inference, optional air-gapped bootstrap for regulated workloads, customer-managed control plane in VPC if required, KMS/HSM integration for keys.
- Hyperscaler concerns: you called out private peering vs public egress, and model artifact transfer constraints when air-gapped.
- Success criteria for eval: low single-digit 99th pct latency at your 1k qps baseline, ability to failover across private peering without data egress, and deterministic startup for offline nodes.

Proposed next tests (we can run these in order):
1) Private-peering throughput test — measure latency / tail at your subnet with a dedicated peering link (30–60 min run).
2) Customer-managed control-plane proof — a short deploy of our control-plane components into a customer VPC (read-only control plane option + audit logs to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver).
3) Air-gap bootstrap test — validate model artifact staging and node bootstrap from an offline media/image.

Attachments: interop-checklist.xlsx (high-level checklist for network/service requirements and what we need from your infra team).

Ask from you:
- Confirm two technical attendees for the deep-dive: Ops lead + security/compliance.
- Are you ok with our proposed test order?
- Availability for the deep-dive: Monday 11/02 or Tuesday 11/03 (30–45m technical session).

I'll loop in Karthik for kernel/quantization notes and Monica for test coordination.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0173

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: on-prem control-plane interoperability (post-demo)

Jordan — thanks for the recap and checklist, that looks useful. Quick answers from our side: 

- Attendees: myself (platform), Ravi Patel (head of TechOps) and Dana (security/compliance). I'll confirm exact names for the deep-dive but those three should be present.
- Test order is fine; priority for us is the air-gap bootstrap proof, then the peering throughput.

Two specific questions we need clarified before the deep-dive: 
1) Customer-managed control plane: can Redwood run the control-plane components entirely inside our VPC with no control traffic crossing the public internet? We need a clear diagram and list of ports.
2) Air-gapped feasibility: is there a supported workflow for fully offline deployment (image-based node bootstrap + signed model artifacts) or would there be any step that requires outbound access (e.g., license checkins)?

We are also evaluating a hyperscaler-managed option and a couple of other inference APIs. Their pitch centers on deeper native VPC integration (private service endpoints) and single-vendor support for KMS. From your experience, what are the common differentiation points we should ask about during the technical session?

Can we target Monday 11/02 10:00am PT for the technical deep-dive?

Best,
Sophia Grant
Director, Platform — FinOps Inc.
sophia@finopsinc.com

Looping in Karthik for feasibility verification. A few suggestions for framing during the deep-dive so the prospect can compare us vs hyperscalers: 

Suggested test matrix (short):
- Test A — Private peering latency: 30 minute steady-state run at 500 qps and 1k qps to show tail behavior.
- Test B — Control plane customer-managed deployment: deploy control-plane components in customer VPC; verify audit log forwarding and that management plane APIs can be locked to a private endpoint.
- Test C — Air-gap bootstrap: bring a node up from offline media, validate signed artifact verification, and then cutover to cluster with no external egress.

Docs to include in the call: proposed-tests.md (I attached a one-pager with what we need from their infra team: IP ranges, firewall rules, KMS policy).

Karthik — can you confirm:
- Supported KMS/HSM integrations (AWS KMS, external HSM via PKCS11?).
- Any quantization/kernel compatibility issues for the models they mentioned (Triton/backends vs our runtime).

I'll coordinate scheduling once Sophia confirms attendees/time.
